% One translated word above one English word. Built from kernel
% primitives, never a tabular, which would break wherever the sheet

  \sbox{\ealboxtr}{\small\textcolor{ealtwocolour}{\ealtext{#2}}}%

    \makebox[0pt][c]{\raisebox{\ealglossraise}{\usebox{\ealboxtr}}}%
  }%
}

\title{Challenge: \ealgloss{Decimals}{ułamki dziesiętne}, \ealgloss{Percentages}{procenty}, and \ealgloss{Fractions}{ułamki}}
\date{}
\maketitle

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{Q\arabic*.}]

\vspace{-3em}

\item Write the following \ealgloss{decimals}{ułamki dziesiętne} as a \ealgloss{fraction}{ułamek} in \ealgloss{simplest form}{najprostszej postaci} and as a \ealgloss{percentage}{procent}:
\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item \( 0.125 \)
    \item \( 0.203125 \)
\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}


\item Convert the following \ealgloss{fractions}{ułamki} into \ealgloss{decimals}{ułamki dziesiętne} and \ealgloss{percentages}{procenty}:
\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item \( \frac{7}{20} \)
    \item \( \frac{33}{320} \)
\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}

\item Express the following \ealgloss{percentages}{procenty} as \ealgloss{decimals}{ułamki dziesiętne} and \ealgloss{fractions}{ułamki} in \ealgloss{simplest form}{najprostszej postaci}:
\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item \( 17.5\% \)
    \item \( 57.8125\% \)
\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}

\end{enumerate}


\bigskip


\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{Q\arabic*.}, start=4]

\item

\textbf{\ealgloss{Basis points}{punkty bazowe}} are units used in finance to describe small changes of \ealgloss{percentages}{procentów}. A \ealgloss{basis point}{punkt bazowy} is a \ealgloss{percent}{procent} of a \ealgloss{percent}{procent}:  
\[
1 \text{ basis point} = 0.01\%
\]

They are often used to describe changes in \ealgloss{interest rates}{stóp procentowych} or \ealgloss{yields}{dochodów}.

For example, an increase of \( 25 \) \ealgloss{basis points}{punktów bazowych} means the \ealgloss{interest rate}{stopa procentowa} goes up by \( 0.25\% \).

\medskip





\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item Write one \ealgloss{basis point}{punkt bazowy} as a \ealgloss{decimal}{ułamek dziesiętny} and a \ealgloss{fraction}{ułamek} in \ealgloss{simplest form}{najprostszej postaci}.
    \item Write 175 \ealgloss{basis points}{punktów bazowych} as a \ealgloss{decimal}{ułamek dziesiętny} and a \ealgloss{fraction}{ułamek} in \ealgloss{simplest form}{najprostszej postaci}.
\end{enumerate}

\bigskip
    \textbf{\ealgloss{Gilts}{brytyjskie obligacje skarbowe}} are UK government \ealgloss{bonds}{obligacje}. When you buy a \ealgloss{gilt}{brytyjską obligację skarbową}, you are lending money to the government.  

    The UK government currently issues 30-year \ealgloss{gilts}{brytyjskie obligacje skarbowe} offering a simple \ealgloss{return}{zwrot} (not \ealgloss{compounding}{kapitalizowanie}) of $5.678\%$ per year. 

    They use these to borrow money to fund investment. Each year they pay a \textbf{\ealgloss{coupon}{kupon}} equal to $5.678\%$ of the amount borrowed. At the end of the 30 years they pay back the original amount borrowed. 
    
    Other durations (1-year, 5-year, 10-year) of \ealgloss{Gilts}{brytyjskich obligacji skarbowych} are also sold.

\medskip

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*), resume]
    \item Find $5.678\%$ as a \ealgloss{decimal}{ułamek dziesiętny} and a \ealgloss{fraction}{ułamek} in its \ealgloss{simplest form}{najprostszej postaci}.
    \item Calculate the total cost for the government to borrow £1000 over 30 years, including payback of the original amount.
    \item Suppose the \ealgloss{coupon}{kuponu} payment of a 30 year \ealgloss{gilt}{brytyjskiej obligacji skarbowej} rises \( 43.5 \) \ealgloss{basis points}{punktów bazowych}. How much more does it cost the government to borrow £1000 over 30 years?
    \item \ealgloss{Gilts}{brytyjskie obligacje skarbowe} offer only \ealgloss{simple interest}{procent prosty}, how might an investor achieve \ealgloss{compounding}{kapitalizujące} \ealgloss{returns}{zwroty}, while still only investing in \ealgloss{Gilts}{brytyjskie obligacje skarbowe}?
\end{enumerate}

\newpage{}

\item Below is a table of the \ealgloss{yields}{dochodów} for \ealgloss{gilts}{brytyjskich obligacji skarbowych} ranging from 1-5 year \ealgloss{maturity}{terminu wykupu} durations:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
\hline
\textbf{\ealgloss{Maturity}{Termin wykupu}} & \textbf{\ealgloss{Yield}{Dochód} (\%)} \\
\hline
1 Year  & 4.377 \\
2 Year  & 4.474 \\
3 Year  & 4.488 \\
4 Year  & 4.492 \\
5 Year  & 4.544 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item What do you notice about the \ealgloss{yield}{dochód} as the \ealgloss{maturity}{terminu wykupu} duration increases?
    \item Assume that \ealgloss{yields}{dochody} do not change over time. Which \ealgloss{gilt}{brytyjską obligację skarbową} would you recommend to someone looking to get the best \ealgloss{return}{zwrot} over a 5 year period?
    \item Consider your answer to Q4(f). What strategy would you use to achieve \ealgloss{compounding}{kapitalizujące} \ealgloss{returns}{zwroty} over a 5 year period?
    \item Implement your strategy, assuming you have £10,000 to invest, at the end of 5 years any \ealgloss{gilts}{brytyjskie obligacje skarbowe} you have bought must have reached \ealgloss{maturity}{termin wykupu}.
    \\
    Clearly indicate which \ealgloss{gilts}{brytyjskie obligacje skarbowe} you would buy at the start of the first year, the start of the second, etc. You may not need all the entries in the table \\
    Round all \ealgloss{coupon}{kuponów} payments down to the nearest pence. \\
    A spare table has been provided.
